title: Pixel Loom

title: Kata Persona Forge
tagline: A character, from the inside out.
features: Adjustable closed-mouth smile, frown and brow expressions with neutral reset
Coherent cheek movement and gentle smile squint alongside independent blink and gaze
Four original editable expression targets on the human and fitted brows
Independent anatomical left/right blink controls with neutral reset
Bounded horizontal/vertical gaze with fitted lids, lashes, iris and cornea
Ten original editable eye targets and blink/gaze interaction correctives
Three distinct adult face presets plus the preserved original three
Nine additional fitted face controls, from head proportions to lips
CC0 MakeHuman anatomical adult with original portrait detail maps
Neutral studio lighting, iris tint and reflective cornea
Fitted brows and lashes with facial morphs
Textured swept short crop and bald option
53-bone weighted skeleton and four static bone-driven poses
Optional original A-line skirt with nine garment-only auxiliary bones
Hem-sway control, body-build fit morphs and editable garment export
Twenty-eight editable appearance morph targets plus pose correctives
Height scaling and preserved garment/pose fixes
Locally bundled Three.js and labeled software preview
Body and close face inspection with profile framing
PNG preview and editable project downloads
description: A local-first character workshop with distinct adult faces, adjustable smile, frown and brow expressions, independent blink and gaze, an optional rigged A-line skirt, weighted posing and editable GLB export.
projectNotes: Inspired by Character Creator 5. Original independent educational kata, without affiliation, endorsement or proprietary file compatibility.

One CC0 anatomical adult with a 2048px skin texture, 1024px eyes, weighted 53-bone skeleton and twenty-eight appearance morph targets plus three pose corrective morphs. Nine new paired face controls shape head width and height, cheeks, chin, nose width and projection, eye spacing, brow height and lips. Angular/Vale, Rounded/Marlowe and Long/Ellis join the preserved Explorer, Pilot and Botanist presets. The neutral original portrait and existing body/garment buffers are preserved. This remains a stylized single-foundation tool, not a demographic library or photoreal production character system. Portrait detail maps are original synthetic detail and tints of one diffuse skin source.

Neutral, T-pose, Hello and Stride are bone-driven static poses, not a walk cycle. Outfit, trousers, fitted brows/lashes and optional textured short crop are separate meshes. Hair is stylized procedural geometry, not a photorealistic production groom. No production facial-expression rig, mouth interior, jaw opening, lip-sync, strand hair, cloth simulation, external mesh import or Reallusion format support. Pose correctives preserve joint volume but remain approximate at appearance extremes. Extreme shapes may need collision and rig-fit adjustment.

GLB export retains UV textures, shape keys, weights, bones, pose clips and the selected appearance. The original foundation export was re-imported and edited in Blender 4.3.2; its Khronos validation reported zero errors and four documented warnings. The distinct-face release was separately checked in Blender 5.2.3 using the exact final software-browser export: all 18 added targets on eight fitted meshes, 53 bones, four clips, materials and embedded images remained editable. The earlier validation result is historical, not a new validator result for this release.

Work stays in your browser. Autosave is best effort; download editable project backups. Undo history does not survive reload. Version-1 migration is explicitly approximate: validated original parameters and the old autosave are retained, but original geometry is not recreated.

The WebGL portrait was tested on Apple M1 hardware over localhost HTTP, including neutral studio lighting, iris tint and reflective cornea. The software preview renders the same human with reduced lighting and resolution; exported assets retain full detail. Other GPU/browser combinations and low-powered-device performance remain unverified. Narrow-layout checks are desktop-browser tests, not physical-device tests.

The distinct-face runtime GLB is approximately 23 MB. Larger morph data adds loading and memory cost. Local Apple M1 WebGL and software-preview checks covered presets, angles, fitted parts and sampled control extremes; they do not prove every possible combination is collision-free. Combined extremes are deliberately exaggerated and need artistic review. The distinct-face milestone added identity shapes; the later eye and closed-mouth expression prototypes are described separately below.

The optional original A-line skirt adds nine garment-only auxiliary bones beneath the pelvis while preserving all 53 body bones, their original weights and the four static body poses. Skirt exports contain 62 total joints and omit trousers; trousers exports omit the skirt and its auxiliary bones. Hem sway and Body build fit morphs are editable and saved with the project. This is bone posing, not cloth simulation: there is no dynamics, collision solver, wind, material thickness or motion playback, and arbitrary bone edits may clip. The actual browser-exported skirt rig was re-imported in Blender 5.2.3; editing a garment bone moved the skirt without moving the body. Existing facial targets, materials, textures and pose clips remain editable. Old projects open with trousers and neutral sway. Sampled fit checks cover supported static poses and tested body shapes, not every possible animation or continuous parameter combination. See docs/QA-SKIRT.md in the app repository.

Independent anatomical left/right blink and bounded horizontal/vertical gaze are eye-only morph posing, not a production facial rig. Ten original editable eye targets include blink/gaze interaction correctives fitted to lids, lashes, eyes, iris and cornea. The expression milestone adds closed-mouth posing; there is no lip-sync, automatic blink timing or new facial animation clips. Eyelids can look heavy or stretched at extreme identity combinations. Exported eye targets are fitted to the saved identity; changing identity in Blender may require refitting. Named per-mesh shape keys remain editable, but the export does not retain the app fitting function or a unified Blender control panel. See docs/QA-BLINK-GAZE.md in the app repository.

Four adjustable closed-mouth expression sliders add Smile, Frown, Raise brows and Furrow brows, with neutral reset, coherent cheek motion and gentle smile squint alongside independent blink and gaze. Opposing controls subtract; equal values cancel. Four original editable targets are retained on the human and fitted brows, with independent eye weights and static pose clips. Expression fields survive undo/redo, autosave and project save/open; old projects load neutral. This is not a production facial rig or muscle solver: no mouth interior, teeth, tongue, jaw opening, wrinkle maps, lip-sync, asymmetric smile or automatic timing. Strong expressions are stylized, especially at extreme identities. Blender edits do not automatically recompute smile squint or opposing-key cancellation; preserve or manually adjust the exported eye weights. Targets fit the saved identity and arbitrary collision freedom is not guaranteed. See docs/QA-EXPRESSIONS.md in the app repository.
